name: May-Hegglin anomaly

criteria.description: Presence of giant platelets on peripheral blood smear
Identification of Döhle-like inclusion bodies in neutrophils
Persistent thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically between 20,000 and 100,000/µL
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Detection of pathogenic variants in the MYH9 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of thrombocytopenia with giant platelets and Döhle-like inclusion bodies in neutrophils, supported by family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for MYH9 mutations confirms diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and hematological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in granulocytes
searchTerms: small inclusions in white blood cells

pathognomonic.notes: Platelets significantly larger than normal on blood smear
Low platelet counts leading to bleeding tendency

common.notes: Easy bruising, epistaxis, and gingival bleeding
searchTerms: mild bleeding from skin and mucous membranes

common.symptomName: Leukocyte inclusion bodies visible on blood smear
common.notes: Visible inclusions in neutrophils and sometimes monocytes
Mild enlargement of the spleen in some patients
Occasionally observed due to bleeding or marrow involvement

occasional.notes: Reported in some patients with MYH9-related disorders
Progressive nephropathy may develop in a subset
Lens opacities reported in some affected individuals
Secondary to mild anemia or chronic bleeding
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.notes: End-stage renal disease in advanced cases
Rare but possible severe hemorrhagic events
Intracranial hemorrhage is rare but serious

laboratory: Giant platelets on peripheral blood smear
imaging: Renal ultrasound in cases with nephropathy
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Absent or reduced platelet glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex
Normal leukocyte morphology without inclusion bodies
Progressive renal failure and sensorineural hearing loss
Characteristic basement membrane abnormalities on renal biopsy
MYH9-related disorder with thrombocytopenia and nephritis
More severe renal involvement than May-Hegglin
Presence of giant platelets and leukocyte inclusions

references: Balduini CL, Pecci A. MYH9-related platelet disorders. Semin Thromb Hemost. 2012;38(6):621-630.
Nurden AT. MYH9 disorders: a clinical perspective. Platelets. 2011;22(7):564-573.
